facts.statement: The genus Plateosaurus was described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
facts.quote: authority: von Meyer, 1837

facts.statement: More than 100 skeletons of Plateosaurus have been found.
facts.quote: over 100 skeletons have been found

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic epoch, approximately 214 to 204 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived during the Late Triassic epoch of the Triassic period, around 214 to 204 million years ago

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived in what is now Central and Northern Europe.
facts.quote: in what is now Central and Northern Europe

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, often referred to as a prosauropod.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus is a basal (early) sauropodomorph dinosaur, a so-called "prosauropod".

facts.statement: The type species of Plateosaurus is Plateosaurus trossingensis.
facts.quote: The type species is Plateosaurus trossingensis

facts.statement: There are currently three valid species of Plateosaurus: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
facts.quote: Currently, there are three valid species; in addition to P. trossingensis, P. longiceps and P. gracilis are also known.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivore

facts.statement: Fully grown Plateosaurus individuals ranged from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and weighed between 600 and 4000 kilograms.
facts.quote: fully grown individuals were between 4.8 and 10 m long and weighed between 600 and 4000 kg

facts.statement: Plateosaurus commonly lived for at least 12 to 20 years.
facts.quote: Commonly, the animals lived for at least 12 to 20 years

facts.statement: Johann Friedrich Engelhardt discovered vertebrae and leg bones of Plateosaurus at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany, in 1834.
facts.quote: In 1834, physician Johann Friedrich Engelhardt discovered some vertebrae and leg bones at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany.

facts.statement: Excavations in a clay pit in Saxony-Anhalt between the 1910s and 1930s revealed between 39 and 50 Plateosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: Between the 1910s and 1930s, excavations in a clay pit in Saxony-Anhalt revealed between 39 and 50 skeletons that belonged to Plateosaurus

facts.statement: Plateosaurus skeletons in a clay pit in Frick, Switzerland, were first noticed in 1976.
facts.quote: The Plateosaurus skeletons in a clay pit of the Tonwerke Keller AG in Frick, Switzerland, were first noticed in 1976.

facts.statement: Fossils referred to Plateosaurus were found in East Greenland but were reclassified into the genus Issi in 2021.
facts.quote: Material referred to Plateosaurus has also been found in the Fleming Fjord Formation of East Greenland, but they were given the new genus name Issi in 2021.

facts.statement: The original 1837 description by von Meyer did not include an explanation for the name Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: Von Meyer's original short description from 1837 did not provide an etymology for Plateosaurus

facts.statement: As of 2019, only three species of Plateosaurus are universally accepted as valid: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
facts.quote: As of 2019, only three species are universally accepted as valid: the type species P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis

facts.statement: Markus Moser considered the genus Sellosaurus to be the same as Plateosaurus but did not determine if S. gracilis and P. engelhardti are the same species.
facts.quote: Moser considered Sellosaurus to be the same genus as Plateosaurus, but did not discuss whether S. gracilis and P. engelhardti belong to the same species.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Adam Yates questioned the separation of the genus Sellosaurus from Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: Palaeontologist Adam Yates of the University of the Witwatersrand cast further doubt on the generic separation.

facts.statement: Adam Yates suggested that P. gracilis might be a metataxon, meaning the material assigned to it may belong to multiple species rather than one.
facts.quote: Yates has cautioned that P. gracilis may be a metataxon, which means that there is neither evidence that the material assigned to it is monophyletic (belongs to one species), nor that it is paraphyletic (belongs to several species).

facts.statement: Most named species of Plateosaurus, except P. gracilis and P. longiceps, are now considered junior synonyms or invalid names.
facts.quote: All named species of Plateosaurus except the type species, P. gracilis, or P. longiceps have turned out to be junior synonyms of the type species or invalid names.

facts.statement: The skull of specimen AMNH FARB 6810, the best-preserved Plateosaurus skull, was redescribed in 2011.
facts.quote: The skull of AMNH FARB 6810, the best-preserved skull of Plateosaurus that has been taken apart during preparation and is thus available as separate bones, was described anew in 2011.

facts.statement: It is debated whether much prosauropod material from the German Knollenmergel labeled as Plateosaurus actually belongs to the type species or to Plateosaurus at all.
facts.quote: Aside from fossils clearly belonging to Plateosaurus, there is much prosauropod material from the German Knollenmergel in museum collections, most of it labeled as Plateosaurus, that does not belong to the type species and possibly not to Plateosaurus at all.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had proportionally long lower legs and metatarsi, indicating it could run quickly on its hind limbs.
facts.quote: The proportionally long lower leg and metatarsus show that Plateosaurus could run quickly on its hind limbs.

facts.statement: The skull of Plateosaurus was small, narrow, and rectangular in side view, nearly three times as long as it was high.
facts.quote: The skull of Plateosaurus is small and narrow, rectangular in side view, and nearly three times as long as it is high.

facts.statement: Features of its teeth and jaw suggest Plateosaurus fed primarily or exclusively on plants.
facts.quote: These features suggest that it fed primarily to exclusively on plants.

facts.statement: The air exchange volume for a P. engelhardti individual estimated to weigh 690 kg was determined to be approximately 20 liters, or 29 mL per kilogram of body weight.
facts.quote: The difference in volume between these two positions defines the air exchange volume (the amount of air moved with each breath), determined to be approximately 20 L for a P. engelhardti individual estimated to have weighed 690 kg, or 29 mL/kg bodyweight.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus probably had an avian-style flow-through lung, though indicators of air sacs invading bones were only recognized in 2010 and found on few individuals.
facts.quote: This is a typical value for birds, but not for mammals, and indicates that Plateosaurus probably had an avian-style flow-through lung, although indicators for postcranial pneumaticity (air sacs of the lung invading the bones to reduce weight) can be found on the bones of only a few individuals, and were only recognised in 2010.

facts.statement: Combined with bone histology evidence, Plateosaurus is indicated to have been endothermic.
facts.quote: Combined with evidence from bone histology this indicates that Plateosaurus was endothermic.

facts.statement: Adults of the type species P. trossingensis reached 4.8 to 10 meters in length and ranged in mass from 600 to 4000 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adults of this species reached 4.8 to 10 m in length, and ranged in mass from 600 to 4000 kg.

facts.statement: The older species P. gracilis was smaller, with a total length of 4 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: The geologically older species, P. gracilis (formerly named Sellosaurus gracilis), was somewhat smaller, with a total length of 4 to 5 m.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was the first "prosauropod" described and serves as the type genus for the family Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus was the first "prosauropod" to be described, and gives its name to the family Plateosauridae as the type genus.

facts.statement: The family Plateosauridae was proposed by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1895 within Theropoda.
facts.quote: Plateosauridae was proposed by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1895 within Theropoda.

facts.statement: The family Plateosauridae was later moved to "Prosauropoda" by von Huene, a placement accepted by most authors.
facts.quote: Later it was moved to "Prosauropoda" by von Huene, a placement that was accepted by most authors.

facts.statement: Sellosaurus is probably a junior synonym of Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: Of these, Sellosaurus is probably another junior synonym of Plateosaurus.

facts.statement: P. gracilis is found in the Löwenstein Formation (lower to middle Norian), while P. trossingensis and P. longiceps come from the Trossingen Formation (upper Norian).
facts.quote: Plateosaurus gracilis, the older species, is found in the Löwenstein Formation (lower to middle Norian). P. trossingensis and P. longiceps stem from the Trossingen Formation (upper Norian) and equivalently aged rock units.

facts.statement: Some researchers debate whether plateosaurs were the direct ancestors of sauropods.
facts.quote: Some researchers do not agree that plateosaurs were the direct ancestors of sauropods.

facts.statement: The lack of forelimb pronation meant Plateosaurus was an obligate biped, unable to walk in any other way.
facts.quote: The lack of forelimb pronation meant that Plateosaurus was an obligate (i.e. unable to walk in any other way) biped.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus possessed teeth where the crown was wider than the root, resembling those of modern herbivorous or omnivorous reptiles.
facts.quote: The maximum width of the crown was greater than that of the root for the teeth of most "prosauropods", including Plateosaurus

facts.statement: Paul Barrett hypothesized that Plateosaurus may have been an omnivore, supplementing its herbivorous diet with small prey or carrion.
facts.quote: Paul Barrett proposed that prosauropods supplemented their mostly herbivorous diets with small prey or carrion, thus making them omnivores.

facts.statement: No fossil of Plateosaurus has yet been discovered containing gastroliths (gizzard stones) in the stomach area.
facts.quote: So far, no fossil of Plateosaurus has been found with gastroliths (gizzard stones) in the stomach area.

facts.statement: Pathologies found on the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200 are hypothesized to result from capture myopathy caused by getting trapped in mud.
facts.quote: Pathologies affecting the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200 have been hypothesized to be the result of capture myopathy, induced by a mud-miring trap.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus exhibited a growth pattern similar to sauropods but with variable rates and final sizes, likely influenced by environmental factors like food availability.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus followed a trajectory similar to sauropods, but with a varied growth rate and final size as seen in extant reptiles, probably in response to environmental factors such as food availability.

facts.statement: Individual Plateosaurus reached fully grown sizes ranging from 4.8 meters to 10 meters in total length.
facts.quote: Some individuals were fully grown at only 4.8 metres' (16 ft) total length, while others reached 10 m.

facts.statement: The presence of an avian-style lung in Plateosaurus is considered further evidence supporting the hypothesis of endothermy.
facts.quote: A further indication for endothermy is the avian-style lung of Plateosaurus.

facts.statement: Studies by Martin Sander and Nicole Klein indicate that some Plateosaurus individuals were fully grown at 12 years, while others were still growing at 18 or 20 years of age.
facts.quote: Sander and Klein found that some individuals were fully grown at 12 years of age, others were still slowly growing at 20 years, and one individual was still growing rapidly at 18 years.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Superior

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was discovered in 1834 by Johann Friedrich Engelhardt and described three years later by Hermann von Meyer.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1834 por Johann Friedrich Engelhardt y descrito tres años más tarde por Hermann von Meyer

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived between 214 and 204 million years ago in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el período Triásico, hace entre 214 a 204 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Three species of Plateosaurus are currently recognized as valid: Plateosaurus trossingensis (type species), Plateosaurus longiceps, and Plateosaurus gracilis.
facts.quote: Se reconocen como válidas tres especies, la especie tipo desde 2019, Plateosaurus trossingensis del Noriense tardío y el Rhaetiense, Plateosaurus longiceps de edad similar y el levemente más antiguo Plateosaurus gracilis del Noriano inferior.

facts.statement: There is no extended consensus on the taxonomy of Plateosaurus species, as other species have been assigned in the past.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, otras especies han sido asignadas en el pasado, y no hay un consenso extendido sobre la taxonomía de las especies de los plateosáuridos.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with a long mobile neck, blunt sharp teeth for crushing plants, powerful hind legs, short muscular arms, and grasping hands with large claws on three fingers, possibly used for defense and feeding.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus era un herbívoro bípedo con un largo cuello móvil, dientes afilados pero rechonchos para triturar plantas, poderosos miembros traseros, brazos cortos pero musculosos y manos prensiles con grandes garras en tres de sus dedos, posiblemente usadas para defenderse y alimentarse.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus commonly lived at least 12 to 20 years, though its maximum lifespan remains unknown.
facts.quote: Comúnmente, estos animales vivían al menos entre 12 a 20 años, pero su esperanza de vida máxima es desconocida.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivorous dinosaur with a small head, a long flexible neck made of 10 cervical vertebrae, a robust body, and a long tail with at least 40 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus tenía la forma corporal típica de un dinosaurio bípedo herbívoro, un cráneo pequeño, un cuello largo y flexible compuesto de 10 vértebras cervicales, un cuerpo robusto y una larga cola compuesta de al menos 40 vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Despite their short arms, Plateosaurus had a robust constitution with hands adapted for grasping objects.
facts.quote: Aun así, poseían una constitución robusta, con manos adaptadas para tomar objetos.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had a narrow shoulder girdle where the clavicles met in the midline of the body, similar to other basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: La cintura escapular era estrecha, con frecuencia, se la muestra desalineada en las monturas y dibujos de esqueletos, y sus clavículas terminaban tocándose en la línea media del cuerpo, como en otros sauropodomorfos basales.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus walked on its toes with its hind limbs positioned under its body, knees and ankles slightly flexed.
facts.quote: Los miembros posteriores se mantenían bajo el cuerpo, con las rodillas y tobillos levemente flexionados, y el pie era digitígrado, lo que significa que el animal caminaba apoyándose sobre sus dedos.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus could run quickly due to its proportionally long legs and metatarsals.
facts.quote: Las patas proporcionalmente largas y el metatarso muestran que Plateosaurus podía correr rápidamente con sus patas.

facts.statement: The skull of Plateosaurus was small, narrow, and rectangular from the side, nearly three times longer than it was high.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Plateosaurus es pequeño y estrecho, rectangular al ser visto de lado, y casi tres veces más largo que alto.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had small leaf-shaped teeth, with 5 to 6 in the premaxilla, 24 to 30 in the maxilla, and 21 to 28 in the dentary.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas tenían varios dientes pequeños en forma de hoja: de 5 a 6 en el premaxilar, 24 a 30 en el maxilar, y 21 a 28 en el dentario.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had thick, blunt teeth with serrated edges that allowed it to crush plant matter.
facts.quote: Las gruesas coronas romas de los dientes, que contaban con bordes aserrados le permitían triturar la materia vegetal.

facts.statement: The combination of its features suggests Plateosaurus fed mainly or exclusively on plants.
facts.quote: Estos rasgos en conjunto sugieren que se alimentaba principal o exclusivamente de plantas.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus eyes pointed directly to the sides rather than forward, providing complete peripheral vision to watch for predators.
facts.quote: Sus ojos apuntan directamente a los lados, más que al frente, proveyendo una visión periférica completa para vigilar a los posibles depredadores.

facts.statement: Research determined that a Plateosaurus individual weighing an estimated 690 kilograms had an air exchange volume of approximately 20 liters, or 29 ml/kg of body weight.
facts.quote: La diferencia de volumen entre ambas posiciones definen el volumen de aire intercambiado, la cantidad de aire movido en cada respiración, determinándose que serían aproximadamente 20 litros para un individuo de Plateosaurus con un peso estimado en 690 kilogramos, o 29 ml/kg de peso corporal.

facts.statement: This air volume indicates Plateosaurus likely had an avian-like lung air circulation system, implying pneumaticity in its skeleton with air sacs invading the bones to reduce weight.
facts.quote: Este es un valor típico para las aves, pero no para los mamíferos, e indica que Plateosaurus probablemente tenía un sistema de circulación de aire en los pulmones similar al de las aves; esto implicaría que tendría también una neumatización del esqueleto, con sacos aéreos del pulmón invadiendo los huesos que además permitían aligerar su peso.

facts.statement: Evidence for this pneumatic condition was not recognized until 2010 and has only been found in the bones of some individuals.
facts.quote: Los indicios de esta condición no fueron reconocidos sino hasta 2010 y solo se han hallado en los huesos de algunos individuos.

facts.statement: Combined with bone histology evidence, this indicates that Plateosaurus was endothermic.
facts.quote: Combinado con la evidencia de la histología de los huesos esto indica que Plateosaurus era endotermo.
